contradicting_evidence: BTC settled flows remain positive, so institutional-flow evidence is divergent rather than uniformly negative.

Large-alt proxy losses were milder than mid- and small-alt losses, and approximately 53% of large-alt constituents outperformed BTC. Relative resilience does not establish positive absolute participation.
Fear sentiment and localized absorption permit a rebound branch, but neither supplies reliable reversal timing.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Downside pressure is favored to persist through alternating rebound attempts and retests. ETH and the mid- and small-alt proxies appear more vulnerable than a broadly transmitted recovery would imply. Confidence is limited by the lack of a current multi-session confirmation sequence; a durable stabilization could weaken this forecast.
falsification_conditions: BTC and ETH sustain recovery while ETH/BTC stabilizes or strengthens and positive breadth expands beyond isolated large-cap names.
Subsequent settled sessions materially improve ETH flows while BTC inflows persist, with corresponding price and participation improvement.
missing_evidence: Subsequent finalized ETF sessions are unavailable; the latest settled session cannot establish persistent current flow direction.
Repeated breadth, ETH/BTC and price observations are needed to confirm whether weakness persists over several days.
There is no direct evidence that stablecoin supply changes are translating into reduced spot demand.
supporting_evidence: The latest finalized ETF session recorded ETH outflows of $105.5 million against BTC inflows of only $17.2 million, providing no broad flow confirmation.
Stablecoin supply declined 1.17% over seven days and 2.16% over 30 days, a liquidity headwind rather than proof of immediate selling.
ETH/BTC is 0.02884 and declined slightly in the latest hour; ETH also underperformed BTC over the supplied 24h window.
Broad proxy participation is negative, with materially weaker returns and fewer advancers in mid- and small-alt buckets than in large alts.
